concepts.title: Uses of the Neem Tree
concepts.section: Neem Baba, Let us read II
concepts.definition: Neem serves health and farming together: twigs clean teeth, leaves fight germs in measles, bark and flowers make medicines, seed powder shields crops from locusts and termites, and oil goes into soap and toothpaste.
concepts.formula: neem_uses = medicines + crop protection + daily products
concepts.key_idea: Every part of the neem, from leaf to root, has a use, which is why it is called nature's gift.
concepts.textbook_ref: fepr103.txt, Neem Baba, Let us read II

solution_steps.explain: Collect each use of neem as the dialogue mentions it, part by part.
Group the uses under health, farming and daily life.
State in one line why people call neem useful and precious.

concepts.title: Neem Baba: Names and Origins
concepts.section: Neem Baba, Let us read I
concepts.definition: The neem tree was born millions of years ago in North India or Myanmar and spread across Asia, Africa and parts of America. Its Sanskrit names include Arishta and Nimba, Iranians gave the name Neem, and scientists call it the bitter grace of God and the magic tree.
concepts.key_idea: A name story, from Arishta the healer to Nimb and Neem, carries the tree's fame across languages.
concepts.textbook_ref: fepr103.txt, Neem Baba, Let us read I

solution_steps.explain: Note the birthplace and spread of the tree from the dialogue.

solution_steps.explain: Arrange the names under Sanskrit, Iranian, Hindi and scientist groups.

concepts.title: Reading a Dialogue: Amber and Neem Baba
concepts.definition: The chapter is written as a conversation between a child and a tree that speaks; questions by Amber pull out facts one by one, which is how a dialogue text organises information.
concepts.key_idea: In a dialogue, each speaker's turn gives one new fact; following the turns gives the whole picture.
concepts.textbook_ref: fepr103.txt, Neem Baba, Let us read

solution_steps.explain: Name who speaks and what each one wants from the talk.
Track how one question leads to one new fact in each turn.
State what the child learns by the end of the conversation.

concepts.title: Word Meanings: Twigs, Measles and Stagnant
concepts.definition: Context gives the meanings: twigs are small thin branches, measles is a disease with fever and red spots, stagnant water is water that does not flow, and purifies means removes harmful particles.
concepts.key_idea: Gloss pairs in the margin mirror the clues inside the sentence, so meaning can be checked both ways.
concepts.textbook_ref: fepr103.txt, Neem Baba, Let us learn
question_patterns: what are twigs according to the chapter

solution_steps.action: find the word in its line
solution_steps.explain: Locate the sentence where the new word appears.
Read before and after the word to see what sense the sentence needs.
Swap in the guessed meaning; if the sentence still makes sense, the meaning is right.

worked_examples.question_pattern: How does neem seed powder help rice farmers?

solution_template.explain: Neem Baba explains that seed powder mixed with water is sprayed on plants.
Locusts stop eating the crop, mosquito breeding falls in standing water, and termites are kept away.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Why is the name Arishta suitable for the neem tree?

solution_template.explain: Arishta means the one who cures diseases.

solution_template.action: match it to the tree's work
solution_template.explain: Neem leaves, bark and roots make medicines, so the healer name fits.
